title: 2007 HMMT February Geometry Problem 4
statement: Circle \(\omega\) has radius 5 and is centered at \(O\). Point \(A\) lies outside \(\omega\) such that \(O A=13\). The two tangents to \(\omega\) passing through \(A\) are drawn, and points \(B\) and \(C\) are chosen on them (one on each tangent), such that line \(B C\) is tangent to \(\omega\) and \(\omega\) lies outside triangle \(A B C\). Compute \(A B+A C\) given that \(B C=7\).

solutions.text: 17. Let \(T_{1}, T_{2}\), and \(T_{3}\) denote the points of tangency of \(A B, A C\), and \(B C\) with \(\omega\), respectively. Then \(7=B C=B T_{3}+T_{3} C=B T_{1}+C T_{2}\). By Pythagoras, \(A T_{1}=A T_{2}=\sqrt{13^{2}-5^{2}}=12\). Now note that \(24=A T_{1}+A T_{2}=A B+B T_{1}+A C+C T_{2}=A B+A C+7\).
